answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashable if it is caught duplicating claims or coordinating fraudulent trades. A reputation system then weights votes by bonded stake and verified history, rather than by account count, so a swarm of fresh Sybils cannot create an echo of consensus. The attacker must lock capital in every identity and risk losing it; the crystal-clear cost makes fake identities expensive, while a fable-like backstory alone earns no influence.
